title: As I Was With Moses
summary: William Branham speaks about his divine commission to pray for the sick, recounting the Angel of the Lord's appearance and the two signs given to vindicate his ministry. He encourages the congregation to have faith in Christ's healing power and prays individually for several people, demonstrating the gift of discernment.

title: Testimony
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of healings, including an elderly congressman and Apache Indians, and preaches on faith and the Holy Spirit's work. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and encourages the audience to believe in divine healing.

title: Believest Thou This?
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of taking God at His Word, using the examples of Mary and Martha from John 11. He contrasts childlike faith with doubt and emphasizes the need for a living, present-tense relationship with God rather than relying on past experiences.

title: Who Has Believed Our Report?
summary: William Branham delivers a closing sermon in Hammond, Indiana, emphasizing faith in Jesus Christ as the same yesterday, today, and forever. He reads from Isaiah 53, declares that healing is already provided through the atonement, and demonstrates the Holy Spirit's presence through discernment and prayer for the sick.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Elijah
summary: William Branham preaches on the Shunammite woman's faith and persistence in seeking the prophet Elisha when her son died. He emphasizes the importance of going forward in faith, not slacking, and trusting God's servants. The sermon encourages believers to maintain their faith even when circumstances seem hopeless.
themes: the power of God through His prophets

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that the same signs and wonders that accompanied Jesus in the Bible should be present in the church today. He calls believers to contend for the faith once delivered to the saints, which includes divine healing and the operation of spiritual gifts.

title: What Is That In Thy Hand?
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of God to use whatever we have in our hands, using the examples of Moses' rod and David's sling. He encourages believers to trust God's promises and step out in faith, even with seemingly small resources.

title: What Is That In Your Hand?
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Moses and the burning bush, emphasizing that God can use whatever we have in our hand, no matter how insignificant, when we surrender it to Him. He encourages believers to turn aside from criticism and approach God reverently, allowing Him to transform their failures into victories.

title: Contending for the Faith
summary: William Branham speaks on contending for the faith once delivered to the saints, emphasizing that true faith is not in creeds or denominations but in a personal relationship with Jesus Christ, who is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He shares testimonies of healing and calls believers to earnestly contend for the apostolic faith, demonstrated through signs and wonders.

title: Being Led of the Holy Spirit
summary: William Branham shares a vision about his future ministry, emphasizing the need to keep supernatural matters private to avoid carnal impersonations. He then preaches on being led by the Holy Spirit, using the examples of Simeon, Mary, and Joseph to illustrate faith and obedience to God's Word.
themes: Being led by the Holy Spirit
The power of the shed blood
The role of women in the Spirit

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on God as Jehovah-Jireh, the Lord who provides, using the story of Abraham and Isaac on Mount Moriah. He emphasizes that God provides a sacrifice for sin and healing, and that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, working through the Holy Spirit in the Church.

title: Sirs, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham opens a series of meetings in Cleveland, Tennessee, emphasizing the importance of seeing Jesus through the Word and the Holy Spirit. He discusses the nature of sin as unbelief, the finished work of Calvary for healing, and the necessity of the supernatural confirmation of the Gospel. He challenges believers to live up to the promises of Christ, who is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
themes: Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
the supernatural confirmation of the Gospel

title: When Divine Love Is Projected, Sovereign Grace Takes Its Place
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of divine love and sovereign grace, using John 3:16 as his text. He shares personal stories and testimonies to illustrate how projecting love in faith allows God's grace to intervene in impossible situations, including healings and deliverances.

title: A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham preaches on the queen of Sheba's journey to witness Solomon's God-given gift, contrasting her faith with the unbelief of Jesus' generation. He emphasizes that divine healing comes through faith in God's Word and that the same Holy Spirit works today through gifts of discernment and healing, calling believers to press in and believe.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Jesus, emphasizing the need to hear Christ above the law and justice represented by Moses and Elijah. He calls for unity and love among believers, urging them to stand for Jesus so that He will stand for them in heaven.

title: God Keeps His Word
summary: William Branham preaches on God's faithfulness to His Word, using the examples of Israel's deliverance from Egypt and the testing at Kadesh-barnea. He warns that the Church must stay true to the Word and be ready for Christ's return, as judgment is coming upon nations that reject God.

title: And Their Eyes Were Opened And They Knew Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He demonstrates the living presence of Christ through the gift of discernment and healing, calling the congregation to recognize and believe in the risen Lord.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Christ, emphasizing that God the Father declared 'This is my beloved Son; hear ye him.' He contrasts the law (Moses) and justice (Elijah) with the mercy and love of Christ, and calls the church to obedience and separation from worldliness.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit as Tutor

title: Thirsting for Life
summary: William Branham preaches on the soul's thirst for God, contrasting perverted worldly pleasures with the true life found in Christ. He shares personal testimonies of healing and prophecy, and calls sinners to accept Christ as Savior, emphasizing that salvation is a finished work at Calvary.
themes: divine healing as part of atonement

title: Expectations And Leadings Of The Spirit
summary: William Branham speaks on the expectations and leadings of the Holy Spirit, using the example of Simeon and Anna who were led by the Spirit to recognize the infant Jesus in the temple. He emphasizes that God reveals Himself to those who are expecting and longing for Him, and that the same Holy Spirit leads believers today.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses biblical examples from John 1 and John 4 to show how Jesus revealed Himself to Jews and Samaritans through supernatural knowledge, and argues that the same manifestations should be expected in the Gentile age. Branham encourages believers to have faith in Christ's finished work and to confess His promises.

title: Will The Church Go Before The Tribulation?
summary: William Branham preaches on the urgency of the end times, drawing parallels between the days of Noah and Lot and the present age. He emphasizes that God sends a message of mercy before judgment, and the Church must escape the coming tribulation through the Rapture.
themes: The revealing of the Son of Man

title: Faith
summary: William Branham speaks on the nature of faith, emphasizing that faith is the purchasing power of healing and that true faith comes from a personal experience with God. He uses biblical examples such as David and Goliath, Moses, and the woman with the issue of blood to illustrate that faith is not intellectual but experiential. He calls the congregation to conduct themselves as sons and daughters of God, especially in the end times.

title: Door to the Heart
summary: William Branham speaks on Revelation 3:20, emphasizing that Christ stands at the door of the heart and knocks. He warns against the Laodicean church age condition of being spiritually poor, blind, and naked while thinking they are rich. Branham urges believers to open every door of their heart to Christ, including private life, selfishness, prejudice, and faith, allowing Him to be Lord and Ruler.
themes: Christ knocking at the heart's door

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, using Hebrews 13:8 as his text. He emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that His works and signs, such as discerning thoughts and revealing secrets, continue through the Holy Spirit in the Church today. Branham calls believers to recognize Christ's presence and power in the closing Gentile age.

title: Behold, I Stand at the Door and Knock
summary: William Branham preaches on the Laodicean Church Age from Revelation 3:20, emphasizing that Christ stands at the door of the heart and knocks, but the latch is on the inside. He illustrates how believers often let Jesus in only partially, keeping doors closed to their private life, selfishness, pride, and faith. Branham calls for full surrender to Christ as Lord, not just Savior, and warns against spiritual blindness that prevents recognizing God's presence and power.
themes: Christ knocking at the heart's door
full surrender to Christ as Lord

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on Hebrews 13:8 and John 12:20, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He argues that the same works Jesus did—such as revealing the secrets of hearts—should be manifest in the Church today through the Holy Spirit, as a sign of the closing Gentile dispensation.
tags: Jesus Christ same yesterday today forever
themes: The Holy Spirit's work in the Church
The closing of the Gentile age

title: The Queen of the South
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom, contrasting her faith and sacrifice with the unbelief of his generation. He emphasizes that a greater than Solomon, Jesus Christ, is present with the same power and gifts, and that people must seek God earnestly despite opposition.
themes: The sign of Jonah and the resurrection

title: Ye Must Be Born Again
summary: William Branham speaks to ministers and believers about the necessity of the new birth, emphasizing that it is more than outward religious experiences or denominational affiliation. He uses the analogy of creation and the Holy Spirit brooding over the earth to illustrate how God brings forth life and how the new birth imparts eternal life that transcends physical decay.

title: But From The Beginning It Was Not So
summary: William Branham preaches on the danger of human traditions replacing God's commandments, using Jesus' rebuke of the Pharisees as a foundation. He calls the church to return to the original Pentecostal experience rather than relying on denominational creeds. The sermon emphasizes that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that true salvation comes through a personal encounter with Christ, not through church membership or rituals.
themes: Personal experience of the Holy Spirit

title: God-Called Man
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of God-called, God-trained men for revival. Using the story of Elisha and Elijah, he emphasizes crossing Jordan (separation from the world) and being molded by God rather than relying on theological education.

title: The Sudden, Secret Going Away of the Church
summary: William Branham preaches on the sudden, secret rapture of the Church, warning believers to be ready at all times. He uses the analogy of the Pearl Harbor attack to illustrate how the world ignores warnings of Christ's coming, and emphasizes the need for individual readiness and the filling of the Holy Spirit.
themes: corruption of the world and church

title: Why Little Bethlehem?
summary: William Branham explores the prophetic significance of Bethlehem as the birthplace of Jesus, tracing its lineage through Rahab, Ruth, and David to show God's sovereign choice of the humble over the great. He emphasizes that Bethlehem, meaning 'House of Bread,' was the fitting birthplace for Christ, the Bread of Life, and draws parallels to the faithful remnant church today.
themes: Typology of Christ in the Old Testament

title: New Ministry
summary: William Branham shares his birthday and introduces a new phase of his ministry focused on praying for the sick without necessarily having visions. He recounts a vision from four years ago that foretold this change and testifies to the healing of a baby named Ricky. He then prays for a prayer line, demonstrating the new approach.

title: El-Shaddai
summary: William Branham preaches on God's covenant with Abraham, emphasizing that God is El Shaddai, the all-sufficient One who pours His strength into believers. He contrasts intellectual faith with heart faith, and calls the church to a revival that throws out dross and reflects Christ.

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham opens a three-day meeting in San Jose, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He explains that the same signs that identified Jesus as the Messiah—such as knowing people's hearts and revealing secrets—should be expected in the Church today through the Holy Spirit. Branham calls believers to look beyond programs and denominations to see Jesus manifested in His Church.

title: What Hearest Thou, Elijah?
summary: William Branham speaks on the need for the church to wait upon God and hear His still small voice, using the story of Elijah after Mount Carmel. He contrasts noisy, sensational religion with the quiet, transformative power of God's voice, urging believers to seek personal encounters with God rather than relying on denominations or big movements.

title: Where Has Thy Strength Gone, Samson?
summary: William Branham uses the story of Samson and Delilah as an allegory for the modern church, warning against flirting with the world and losing spiritual power through organization, intellectualism, and worldliness. He calls for a return to the Holy Ghost, old-fashioned revival, and the new birth experience.

title: IT IS I, BE NOT AFRAID
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus walking on water and telling his disciples 'It is I; be not afraid.' He emphasizes that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that the Holy Spirit is present to heal and save. He calls believers to not be afraid of the Spirit's work, but to accept it as their only hope.

title: As The Eagle Stirreth Up Her Nest
summary: William Branham preaches on Deuteronomy 32:11, comparing the Church to an eagle. He describes the eagle's unique characteristics—its high nest, keen vision, and renewal of youth—as symbols of the believer's life in Christ. Branham urges Christians to rise above worldly entanglements and stand on the unshakable Rock of Ages.
themes: Eagle as symbol of the Church

title: A Prophet Like Unto Moses
summary: William Branham speaks on the need for the Church to recognize the living presence of Christ through the Holy Spirit, using the account of Jesus walking on water to illustrate how believers often fail to see Him in their midst. He emphasizes that the same miracles Jesus performed are available today through faith, and calls for unity among believers in preparation for the Second Coming.
themes: The Church as the Body of Christ

title: Who Is This?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question asked by the people of Jerusalem when Jesus entered the city: 'Who is this?' He draws parallels between the first coming of Christ and the latter-day outpouring of the Holy Spirit, emphasizing that the same Spirit that worked in Jesus is working today through signs, wonders, and the gathering of believers. Branham encourages the congregation to know Christ personally and to believe in His promises despite the world's confusion.

title: What Was The Holy Ghost Given For?
summary: William Branham teaches on the purpose of the Holy Spirit, explaining that God sent the Holy Spirit to dwell in His Church and continue His work through believers. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is God Himself living in the Church, restoring fellowship lost in Eden, and preparing the Bride for the Rapture.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Jesus, emphasizing the need to hear and obey Christ alone. He contrasts the law of Moses and the prophets with the gospel of Jesus, and calls the church to be filled with the Holy Spirit and do the works of Christ.

title: IT IS I, BE NOT AFRAID
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus walking on water and calming the disciples' fear, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers to have faith in God's promises and to recognize the Holy Spirit's presence in the church today.

title: Hearing, Receiving, And Acting
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of hearing God's Word, recognizing it as truth, and acting upon it. He contrasts the carnal believer (represented by Esau) with the spiritual believer (Jacob), emphasizing that true faith requires separation from the world and obedience to God's promises.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of hearing and obeying Jesus Christ, using the Mount of Transfiguration as a context. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is the true Tutor of the Church, and calls for repentance from worldliness and a return to old-fashioned holiness.

title: Show Us The Father And It Will Satisfy Us
summary: William Branham preaches on the desire of the human heart to see God, exploring four ways to see Him: in His universe, in His Word, in His Son, and in His people. He uses illustrations from nature and personal experiences to demonstrate God's presence and faithfulness.

title: As I Was With Moses, So I Will Be With Thee
summary: William Branham preaches on Joshua 1, emphasizing God's promise to Joshua that as He was with Moses, so He would be with him. He draws parallels between the natural journey of Israel and the spiritual journey of the Church, urging believers to stay true to God's Word and follow the leading of the Holy Spirit.

title: Revelation, Chapter Four Part III
summary: In this sermon, William Branham continues his exposition of Revelation chapter 4, focusing on the throne of God and the mercy seat. He emphasizes that the mercy seat becomes a judgment seat after the Church is raptured, and that only the Blood of Jesus Christ can appease God's wrath. He also shares testimonies of answered prayer and discusses the spiritual condition of the world and the Church in the last days.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham returns to Beaumont, Texas after twelve years, emphasizing the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ as the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses the importance of love, faith, and the Holy Spirit, and prepares to pray for the sick, affirming that healing and salvation were accomplished at Calvary.

title: Why?
summary: William Branham delivers a farewell message in Beaumont, Texas, emphasizing love and unity among believers of different denominations. He shares a personal vision where God shows him the cost of sin and the power of forgiveness, leading him to repent of his judgmental attitude. He then preaches from Jeremiah 8:22, asking why people refuse God's provided way of escape through Jesus Christ.
themes: God's provision for healing and salvation

title: Turning Northward
summary: William Branham uses Deuteronomy 2:3 to call the church to move beyond denominational divisions and into the fullness of God's promise. He compares Israel's wilderness wanderings to the Pentecostal movement's forty-year stagnation, urging unity and a return to Spirit-led revival.
themes: the danger of adding to grace
the need for a new generation

title: Sirs, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the need to see Jesus as He is today, the same yesterday, today, and forever. He contrasts the early Pentecostal church's faith with modern complacency, urging believers to recognize God's visitation and return to the Word and Spirit. He emphasizes that the Messiah's sign is a prophet who knows the secrets of the heart, as demonstrated when Jesus called Simon and Nathanael.
themes: Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: IT IS I, BE NOT AFRAID
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages faith in Christ's finished work at Calvary for both salvation and healing, and demonstrates through Scripture how Jesus revealed Himself as Messiah through prophetic signs, which continue today through the Holy Spirit.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Balm in Gilead
summary: William Branham preaches on the question from Jeremiah 8:22, asking why God's people are not recovered if there is balm in Gilead and a physician there. He warns against rejecting God's provision, using examples from Israel's history and contemporary society, and calls the church to holiness and unity.
themes: holiness and separation from the world

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the covenant God made with Abraham, emphasizing that believers are Abraham's Seed through faith in Christ. He explains that God's promises are unconditional and that healing is already provided through Christ's sacrifice. Branham encourages the congregation to look to their Sacrifice rather than their own worthiness.

title: Be Not Afraid
summary: William Branham encourages believers not to fear, using the account of Jesus walking on water. He contrasts the early Pentecostal movement with modern Christianity, emphasizing the need for genuine faith and holiness. Branham also shares testimonies of healings and prophetic ministry, urging the church to prepare for Christ's soon return.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the compound redemptive name Jehovah-Jireh, 'the Lord will provide a sacrifice,' using Abraham's faith as a model for believers. He emphasizes that believers are Abraham's Seed through Christ and must possess Abraham's unwavering faith to claim God's promises, including healing. The sermon also recounts a debate on divine healing and the photographic evidence of the Angel of the Lord.
themes: photographic evidence of Angel of the Lord

title: But It Wasn't So From The Beginning
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of returning to the original Pentecostal experience and warns against hybrid religion that mixes human traditions with God's Word. He uses the analogy of hybrid corn and mules to illustrate how perversion leads to sterility and death, urging believers to be pedigreed Christians tracing their lineage back to Pentecost.

title: Gabriel's Instructions to Daniel
summary: William Branham begins a study on Daniel's Seventy Weeks, explaining its connection to the Book of Revelation and the end times. He emphasizes the need for prayer and understanding as the Church approaches the final week of Daniel's prophecy.

title: It Becometh Us to Fulfil All Righteousness
summary: William Branham, facing his mother's imminent death, preaches on the necessity of fulfilling all righteousness as exemplified by Jesus' baptism. He shares personal testimonies of visions and healings to demonstrate God's faithfulness, urging believers to stand firm on God's Word despite criticism.

title: A True Sign That's Overlooked
summary: William Branham preaches on how God uses prophets as signs to a generation, but these signs are often overlooked. He draws parallels from Noah, Moses, Ezekiel, and Elijah to show that true prophets are rejected by the world but are God's deliverance for His people.

title: Paradox
summary: William Branham discusses the concept of paradox as something incredible but true, using examples from nature and Scripture. He shares a vision of a deadly mamba snake and emphasizes the need for sincerity in faith. The sermon culminates in the account of Joshua commanding the sun to stand still, illustrating God's power over creation.

title: Christianity Versus Idolatry
summary: William Branham contrasts true Christianity with idolatry, tracing its origins from pagan Rome to modern practices. He warns against false spirits and emphasizes the importance of adhering to Scripture, using examples from history and his own ministry.

title: Sirs, We Would See Jesus
summary: In this Christmas message, William Branham contrasts the true meaning of Christmas with its modern commercialization and pagan traditions. He emphasizes that to truly see Jesus, one must die to self and be crucified with Christ, pointing to the cross rather than to celebrations or church affiliations.
themes: The Cross as the Way to See Jesus

title: You Must Be Born Again
summary: William Branham teaches on the necessity of the new birth, emphasizing that it is a spiritual experience beyond church membership or creed recitation. He uses the conversation between Jesus and Nicodemus to explain that being born again is essential to see and enter the Kingdom of God.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: If God Be With Us, Then Where Is All The Miracles?
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for God's people to return to the Word and experience His miracles. Using the story of Gideon, he challenges the church to move beyond denominational barriers and doubt to see God's supernatural power manifested today.
themes: the baptism of the Holy Spirit

title: Presuming
summary: William Branham warns against presuming upon God's grace without actual biblical authority. Using the example of Israel at Kadesh-barnea and Samson, he urges believers to fully obey God's Word rather than relying on past experiences or denominational creeds.
themes: The danger of relying on past experiences
Need for holiness and separation from the world

title: Forsaking All
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of forsaking all to follow Christ, using examples from Scripture such as Abraham, Israel, and the disciples. He emphasizes that God rewards those who leave behind worldly possessions, relationships, and traditions to obey His Word.

title: The Meanest Man I Know
summary: William Branham speaks at a Full Gospel Business Men's Fellowship breakfast, sharing personal experiences of visions and healings, and then preaches on the Pharisee who invited Jesus to dinner, contrasting the world's ways with the humility of Christ.

title: The Spoken Word Is The Original Seed 1
summary: William Branham begins a series explaining his ministry and beliefs, emphasizing that the spoken Word of God is the original seed that cannot be hybridized. He argues that the Bible is the infallible Word of God, that it does not contradict itself, and that adding to or taking from it brings judgment. He traces the pattern of hybridization from Eve to modern denominations, asserting that true life comes only from the original seed.
themes: The Word of God is eternal and cannot be changed
Each generation has its own revival
The Bible is the only standard for judgment
Faith must rest on the Word alone

title: The Restoration of the Bride Tree
summary: William Branham speaks on Easter Sunday about the concept of restoration, using Joel 2:25 and Genesis 20:7 as texts. He explains that believers have the legal right to enforce God's promises against Satan, restoring what was lost through sin, sickness, and death. The sermon emphasizes the power of the Holy Spirit to bring restoration and resurrection.

title: Putting On The Whole Armor Of God
summary: William Branham preaches on Ephesians 6:10-18, emphasizing the need for Christians to put on the whole armor of God to stand against the wiles of the devil. He contrasts the ever-changing weapons of earthly warfare with the unchanging, perfect Word of God, which is the believer's ultimate defense. Branham warns against Satan's tactics of reasoning and misinterpreting Scripture, urging believers to stay fortified behind God's Word.

title: Convinced Then Concerned
summary: William Branham preaches on the need to be convinced of the truth before being concerned for others. He uses the examples of John the Baptist, Andrew, Jacob, and Shamgar to illustrate how conviction leads to action, and laments the lack of concern in the current age due to a lack of conviction.

title: Be Not Afraid
summary: William Branham opens a West Coast campaign in Los Angeles, expressing gratitude for fellowship and recounting a recent gun accident that nearly killed him. He uses the biblical account of Jesus walking on water to encourage believers to be of good cheer and not afraid, emphasizing the importance of being convinced of Christ's divinity and the power of testimony.

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham opens a five-day campaign in Grass Valley, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses the story of the Greeks seeking Jesus and the calling of Nathanael to illustrate that Christ is revealed through the Word and through prophetic discernment, not through creeds or denominations.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
The Word of God as the standard
Divine healing as a sign of Christ's presence
Rejection of creeds that nullify God's Word

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the Abrahamic covenant and the faith of Abraham, emphasizing that believers are Abraham's seed through Christ and must hold fast to God's Word without wavering. He contrasts true faith with emotionalism and denominationalism, calling for complete separation from unbelief and worldly systems.

title: Jehovah-Jireh 3
summary: William Branham continues his series on Abraham, emphasizing the importance of obeying God's Word without reasoning. He contrasts the faith of Abraham with the disobedience of Lot's wife and Eve, and discusses the covenant God made with Abraham and its fulfillment in Christ. Branham also shares testimonies of healing and the work of the Holy Spirit in the meetings.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham opens a revival in Spokane, emphasizing the authority of God's Word and the need to hear Christ alone. He shares testimonies of healing from his overseas ministry and calls believers to die to self and be born again, using the Transfiguration account to highlight that Jesus is God manifested in flesh.

title: Behold, A Greater Than All Of Them Is Here
summary: William Branham preaches on the need to recognize Christ's presence and works, rebuking a generation that fails to see the greater One among them. He emphasizes that true faith is built on the Word and the Spirit's manifestation, and warns against being caged by tradition and organization.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And For Ever
summary: William Branham opens a series of meetings in Salem, Oregon, emphasizing the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ as the same yesterday, today, and forever. He calls for unity among believers, stresses the importance of the Word of God, and explains that divine healing and salvation are already accomplished through Christ's sacrifice, to be received by faith.
themes: Divine healing as a redemptive blessing

title: Behold, A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham contrasts the faith of the Queen of Sheba and the Ninevites with the unbelief of his generation, emphasizing that the sign of the resurrection is given to an adulterous generation. He urges believers to look to Christ rather than symptoms, and warns against rejecting the Holy Spirit's gifts.

title: Sir, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of ministering to Native American tribes, emphasizing simple faith and the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ. He calls believers to see Jesus through the same works He did yesterday, today, and forever, and prepares the congregation for a healing service.

title: A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham preaches on recognizing God's gifts and signs, using the biblical text of Matthew 12:41-42 to contrast the faith of the Queen of Sheba and the Ninevites with the unbelief of Jesus' generation. He emphasizes that Jesus is greater than Solomon and Jonah, and calls believers to simple faith in the resurrected Christ for healing and salvation.
themes: Gifts and offices in the Church

title: Present Stage of My Ministry
summary: William Branham reflects on his ministry, recounting a vision from thirty years ago and its fulfillment. He discusses the separation that comes with standing true to the Word, using Paul and Demas as an example, and explains the different dimensions of existence after death.

title: Countdown
summary: William Branham preaches on the parallels between scientific achievements and spiritual achievements in the church age. He traces the progression from horse and buggy (justification) to automobile (sanctification) to airplane (Pentecostal baptism of the Holy Ghost) and finally to astronaut (the present spiritual age where believers can go beyond denominational thinking). He emphasizes that natural things reflect spiritual realities and that believers must stay true to the Word.

title: Blasphemous Names
summary: William Branham discusses the need for a larger church building, commemorates Brother Taylor, and interprets a sister's dream about the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is poured out on individuals, not organizations, and that true faith requires adding virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness, and love.

title: Investments
summary: William Branham uses the story of the rich young ruler to discuss the concept of spiritual investments, urging believers to invest in eternal life through faith in Christ rather than worldly possessions. He draws parallels to Noah, Daniel, and other biblical figures who trusted God's promises despite opposition.

title: Is This The Sign Of The End, Sir?
summary: William Branham preaches on the urgency of the times, interpreting Revelation 10:1-7 and discussing visions and dreams that point to the end of the age. He shares personal experiences and prophetic insights, emphasizing the need to stay true to the Word and the Spirit's guidance.

title: Accepting God's Provided Way At The End Time
summary: William Branham speaks on accepting God's provided way, using nature as an illustration. He shares a vision of the afterlife and recounts leading an infidel to Christ through a simple lesson about an apple tree. The sermon emphasizes that God has a perfect way for everything, and we must follow it rather than manufacturing our own.

title: The Way of a True Prophet
summary: William Branham uses the prophet Amos as a model to contrast true prophetic ministry with modern evangelism. He warns that the church has drifted from the Word into sin and compromise, and calls for a return to holiness and the authority of Scripture.

title: Identification
summary: William Branham preaches on identifying oneself with Bible characters by looking into the mirror of God's Word. He emphasizes Christ as the perfect example of God's character and calls believers to let that same mind be in them, reflecting Christ in their lives.

title: God Hiding Himself In Simplicity, Then Revealing Himself In The Same
summary: William Branham rededicates the Branham Tabernacle, emphasizing reverence and order in worship. He then introduces a message on how God hides Himself in simplicity, revealing Himself to the humble rather than the wise.

title: The Fourth Seal
summary: William Branham opens the Fourth Seal from Revelation 6:7-8, revealing the pale horse and its rider named Death. He connects this seal to the antichrist spirit and the end-time revelation of mysteries, emphasizing the vindication of God's Word and the stimulation of new wine through revelation.

title: The Fifth Seal
summary: William Branham opens the Fifth Seal from Revelation 6:9-11, revealing the souls under the altar who were slain for the Word of God. He explains that no beast announces this seal because the church age has ended and the antichrist's ride is complete. Branham contrasts the four beasts of God with the four horses of the antichrist, showing how God's power combated each stage of false teaching.
themes: Martyrdom and the souls under the altar

title: Questions and Answers on the Seals
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation regarding the Seven Seals, the wise and foolish virgins, the Rapture, and other biblical topics. He emphasizes the importance of not interpreting revelations personally and encourages believers to continue faithfully in their duties.

title: The World Is Falling Apart
summary: William Branham warns that the world is falling apart due to corruption in politics, education, and religion, including Pentecostalism. He calls for a return to the pure Word of God and the Holy Spirit, rejecting man-made systems and traditions. He emphasizes that only the coming of Jesus Christ can save the world.

title: The Third Exodus
summary: William Branham preaches on the parallel between the exodus of Israel from Egypt and a spiritual exodus of the true church in the last days. He warns against denominationalism and the ecumenical movement, calling believers to separate from organized religion and return to the pure Word and Spirit of God.

title: Token
summary: William Branham preaches on the concept of the 'Token' from Exodus 12:13, explaining that the blood of the lamb in Egypt was a token of God's protection. He draws a parallel to the Holy Spirit as the Token for believers today, emphasizing that it is the only sign God will recognize for salvation and deliverance from coming wrath.

title: He That Is In You
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of God within believers, emphasizing that 'greater is He that is in you than he that is in the world.' He discusses the end times, the Seven Seals, and the importance of staying true to the Word. The sermon includes baby dedications, testimonies of healing, and a call to faith and repentance.
themes: Greater is He that is in you

title: Shalom
summary: William Branham delivers a New Year's message on the theme of 'Shalom' (peace), contrasting the gross darkness covering the earth with the light of God's Word for the elect. He warns against ecumenical movements and denominationalism, urging believers to stand on the vindicated Word and look forward to Christ's coming.

title: Identification
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of spiritual identification, using Bible characters as mirrors for believers to examine their own faith and alignment with God's Word. He emphasizes that true Christians are identified by the Holy Spirit and by their adherence to Scripture, contrasting them with those who follow popular religious trends.

title: When Their Eyes Were Opened, They Knew Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the road to Emmaus story, emphasizing that the disciples failed to recognize the resurrected Jesus because they did not understand the Scriptures. He draws parallels to the present day, where believers often fail to recognize Christ's work because of creeds, programs, and unbelief. Branham urges the congregation to invite Jesus in so He can open their eyes to the promised Word for this age.

title: Possessing The Gate Of The Enemy After Trial
summary: William Branham preaches on Abraham's faith and the promise that his seed would possess the gate of his enemies. He draws parallels between Abraham's test and the believer's trials, emphasizing that the Royal Seed (Christ) has already conquered every enemy—sickness, death, hell—and that believers, as Abraham's spiritual seed, can possess the gates of their enemies through faith in God's Word and the sealing of the Holy Spirit.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the covenant God made with Abraham, emphasizing that God's promises are unconditional and require total separation from unbelief. He draws parallels between the Old Testament covenant and the New Covenant in Christ, highlighting that the same Spirit that was in Christ is in believers today, confirming the covenant through signs and wonders.
themes: the Spirit of Christ in believers

title: Jehovah-Jireh 3
summary: William Branham continues his series on Abraham, focusing on the promise of Isaac and the revelation of God as Elohim. He draws parallels between Abraham's encounter with God in human flesh and the present-day manifestation of God's Word through discernment and healing, emphasizing faith and the imminent return of Christ.

title: Christ Is Identified The Same In All Generations
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He explains that God identifies Himself in each generation by manifesting His Word through prophets, and that the true interpretation of Scripture comes when God makes His promise live. Branham calls believers to recognize the present hour and the promised Word for this age, rather than living in the glare of past revivals.

title: Recognizing Your Day And Its Message
summary: William Branham preaches on recognizing the spiritual hour and message of the day, drawing from Hosea 6 to discuss Israel's restoration and the church's condition. He emphasizes the fulfillment of prophecy, the opening of the Seven Seals, and the imminent Rapture of the Bride.

title: Wedding Ceremony
subtitle: 65-0116X
summary: William Branham officiates the wedding of Marilyn Simpson and Gerald Martens, performing a traditional Christian ceremony with prayers for the couple's future. He then offers brief remarks and blessings, connecting the earthly wedding to the coming of Christ for His Bride.
themes: Symbolism of the Bride of Christ

title: A Paradox
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of paradox—things that seem incredible but are true—using biblical examples such as Joshua commanding the sun to stand still, the virgin birth, and the resurrection. He emphasizes that God's promises are fulfilled through faith, not human effort, and that the same God who performed miracles in the past is still active today.

title: The Seed Of Discrepancy
summary: William Branham preaches on the parable of the wheat and tares from Matthew 13, explaining that the seed of discrepancy (tares) sown by the enemy represents anything contrary to God's Word. He warns against false teachings, organizations, and compromise, emphasizing that only the genuine Word of God, quickened by the Holy Spirit, produces true believers. The harvest at the end of the age will separate the wheat from the tares.

title: The God Who Is Rich In Mercy
summary: William Branham preaches on Ephesians 2, emphasizing God's mercy in quickening those dead in sin. He contrasts true believers (eagles) with impersonators (chickens), using Old Testament examples like Noah, Moses, and the brass serpent to show God's provision for those who follow His Word. He warns against idolizing denominations and calls for a return to the full Word of God.

title: Lean Not Unto Thy Own Understanding
summary: William Branham preaches on Proverbs 3:5, warning against relying on human understanding instead of God's Word. He uses examples from Eden, the Pharisees, and modern churches to show how leaning on creeds and denominations leads to spiritual blindness and death.
themes: The eagle as a symbol of the believer

title: Broken Cisterns
summary: William Branham preaches on Jeremiah 2, contrasting the living water of God with man-made religious systems, which he likens to broken cisterns that cannot hold water. He warns against relying on denominational structures and emphasizes the need for a personal, Spirit-quickened relationship with Christ.

title: Birth Pains
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of birth pains, drawing parallels between natural childbirth and spiritual rebirth. He discusses the necessity of pain and distress for new life, both in individuals and in the world, and interprets current world events as signs of the impending new creation.

title: This Day This Scripture Is Fulfilled
summary: William Branham speaks at a Full Gospel Business Men's Fellowship convention, recounting a recent incident where a misprinted Bible led him to reflect on Luke 4:21, 'This day this Scripture is fulfilled.' He draws parallels between Jesus' ministry and the present day, emphasizing that the signs of the end times, as in the days of Sodom, are being fulfilled before our eyes.
themes: Revelation of the Son of man

title: Doors In Door
summary: William Branham speaks at a Full Gospel Business Men's Fellowship breakfast in Flagstaff, Arizona, sharing personal anecdotes and a message on the Laodicean church age. He emphasizes the importance of every word of God and the need to open the door to Christ, who stands outside the church knocking.

title: A Man Running From The Presence Of The Lord
The Seed Is Not Heir With The Shuck
summary: William Branham preaches on Galatians 4:27-31, using the allegory of Abraham's two sons (Ishmael and Isaac) and the virgin Mary to illustrate three stages of spiritual development: the stalk (Luther), the tassel (Wesley), and the shuck (Pentecost). He argues that denominational systems are merely carriers of the true Seed, which is the full Word of God manifested in a Bride Church in the last days.

title: This Day This Scripture Is Fulfilled
summary: William Branham preaches on the fulfillment of Scripture in the present age, drawing from Jesus' reading of Isaiah 61 in the synagogue. He emphasizes that God interprets His own Word by making it come to pass, and warns against man-made traditions that blind people to God's work. Branham applies this to the current state of the church and world, declaring that the prophecies for this day are being fulfilled.

title: God's Chosen Place of Worship
summary: William Branham preaches on Deuteronomy 16:1-3, arguing that God's chosen place of worship is not a denomination or church but in Jesus Christ alone. He contrasts the law of death from Mount Sinai with the law of life from Mount Calvary, emphasizing that God put His name in His Son, and only through Christ can one truly worship God.

title: Wedding Ceremony
subtitle: 65-0220X
summary: William Branham officiates a wedding ceremony uniting Linda Reliford and Charles Branham at the Branham Tabernacle. He performs the traditional vows and pronounces them husband and wife, then offers a prayer reflecting on marriage as a symbol of the Church's waiting for the Bridegroom.

title: Marriage And Divorce
summary: William Branham teaches on the biblical view of marriage and divorce, emphasizing that God's original plan was one man and one woman for life. He argues that divorce was permitted only because of human hardness of heart, and that the church must return to the beginning for the true answer.

title: Who Is This Melchisedec?
summary: William Branham explores the identity of Melchisedec, arguing that He is God in a theophanic form, the Word before becoming flesh in Jesus Christ. He discusses the concept of en morphe (God changing His form) and the predestination of believers, who were in God's thoughts before the foundation of the world. Branham also contrasts the theophany of Melchisedec with the fleshly existence of believers, who bypass the theophany to be tempted by sin, but will receive a glorified body after death.
themes: Eternal Life and the Book of Life
Resurrection and the earnest of the Spirit
The Word as attribute and expression

title: The Easter Seal
summary: William Branham preaches on the significance of Easter as the seal of Christ's resurrection, emphasizing that the same Spirit that raised Jesus from the dead dwells in believers, quickening them to eternal life and empowering them for this age. He uses the analogy of an eagle and a magnet to illustrate how God's Spirit calls His elect out of denominational systems into the truth of the present hour.

title: It Is The Rising Of The Sun
summary: William Branham preaches on Easter morning about the resurrection of Jesus Christ as the ultimate proof of God's Word. He emphasizes that believers are beneficiaries of Christ's resurrection, quickened by the same Spirit that raised Him, and that the true Gospel is confirmed by the power and manifestation of the Holy Spirit.

title: Does God Ever Change His Mind About His Word?
summary: William Branham preaches on the sovereignty of God's Word, using the story of Balaam to argue that God never changes His mind about His Word. He contrasts the spiritual church (Israel) with organized religion (Moab), warning against denominationalism and emphasizing election and the sealing of the Holy Spirit.
themes: Conflict between spiritual and carnal religion
The sealing of the Holy Spirit

title: One In A Million
summary: William Branham speaks at a breakfast gathering in Los Angeles, sharing testimonies of healing and visions, including a vision of a sword representing the Word and the opening of the Seven Seals. He emphasizes the importance of believing every Word of God and the rarity of true faith, using the analogy of one in a million seeds that come to life.

title: God's Provided Place of Worship
summary: William Branham preaches on Deuteronomy 16, emphasizing that God has chosen one specific place for worship—Jesus Christ. He argues that denominations and creeds are not God's provided place, and that only through being in Christ, by the Holy Spirit, can one truly worship God. Branham calls believers to abandon man-made systems and enter into the Body of Christ.
themes: The Holy Spirit's role in worship

title: Proving His Word
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of proving God's Word through faith and obedience. He uses biblical examples such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, Joshua, and the woman with the issue of blood to illustrate that God always fulfills His promises. He encourages believers to maintain the right attitude and trust in God's Word, regardless of circumstances.

title: Does God Change His Mind?
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of God, using the story of Balaam and Balak to illustrate that while God may permit certain actions, His perfect will and Word remain constant. He contrasts the spiritual church (Israel) with the natural church (Moab), warning against impersonation and emphasizing the need for a living Holy Spirit-led faith.

title: The Seed Shall Not Be Heir With The Shuck
summary: William Branham preaches on Galatians 4:27-31, using the allegory of Abraham's two sons, Ishmael and Isaac, to illustrate that the spiritual church cannot be heir with denominational organizations. He traces the seed through three stages—Hagar (stalk), Sarah (tassel), and Mary (shuck)—to show that only the true Seed, Christ, is the heir, and that the Pentecostal movement, like the shuck, is a carrier but not the Seed itself.

title: The Choosing Of A Bride
summary: William Branham uses the biblical account of Abraham's servant choosing a bride for Isaac as a type of Christ choosing His Bride, the Church. He emphasizes the importance of making right choices in life, particularly in selecting a spouse and a church, and warns against being led astray by worldly attractions. Branham contrasts a marriage based on character versus one based on outward beauty, drawing spiritual parallels to the Church's relationship with Christ.
themes: The Church as the Bride of Christ

title: Ashamed
summary: William Branham shares personal reflections on his recent trip to Africa, the challenges of holding meetings, and the urgency of the last days. He then preaches from Mark 8:34-38 on the importance of not being ashamed of Christ and His words.

title: Ashamed
summary: William Branham shares personal reflections on his recent trip to Africa, the challenges of holding meetings, and the urgency of the last days. He then preaches from Mark 8:34-38 on the importance of not being ashamed of Christ and His words.

title: Trying To Do God A Service Without Being The Will Of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of doing God's will rather than relying on good intentions or popular consensus. Using the example of David bringing the ark of the covenant on a new cart instead of following God's ordained method, he warns against consulting theologians and organizations instead of God. He emphasizes that God reveals His Word in His season and that true service must align with His will.
themes: doing God's will vs. good intentions
the Word of God as the standard

title: Spiritual Food In Due Season
summary: William Branham preaches on the spiritual drought of the last days, using the story of Elijah as a type. He emphasizes that God provides spiritual food for His faithful children in due season, and that the messenger and the message are one when sent with 'Thus Saith the Lord.'

title: The Anointed Ones At The End Time
summary: William Branham preaches on Matthew 24:24, warning that in the end times there will be false anointed ones (false Christs and false prophets) who perform genuine signs and wonders, yet teach false doctrine. He uses the analogy of rain falling on both wheat and tares to explain how the same Holy Spirit can anoint both true and false teachers, emphasizing that the elect cannot be deceived because they are rooted in the Word.

title: What Is The Attraction On The Mountain?
summary: William Branham preaches on the attraction of God fulfilling His Word, using the triumphal entry of Jesus into Jerusalem as a type. He contrasts the faithful who recognize prophecy being fulfilled with the religious leaders who are blind to it, and applies this to the present day where God is again fulfilling His Word in a remarkable way.

title: The God Of This Evil Age
subtitle: 65-0801M
summary: William Branham preaches on the evil age of the last days, contrasting the Holy Spirit calling out a Bride for Christ with the spirit of the devil working in deception. He emphasizes that the world is more evil than ever, and that believers must be called out of this chaos by the vindicated Word of God for this hour.

title: Events Made Clear By Prophecy
summary: William Branham preaches on how Bible prophecy makes future events clear, emphasizing that God's Word is a living revelation of Jesus Christ. He contrasts true believers who accept the Word with those who rely on man's interpretation, and uses examples from Scripture to show how God vindicates His prophets in each age.

title: And Knoweth It Not
summary: William Branham speaks informally to his congregation, reflecting on the Laodicean Church Age and the spiritual blindness of modern Christians. He addresses issues of women's dress, hair, and roles in the church, emphasizing that many are 'naked, miserable, blind, and know it not.' He also shares personal anecdotes and discusses the nature of God and the Church.
themes: The nature of God and Christ
The Church as the Body of Christ
The initial evidence of the Holy Spirit

title: Christ Is Revealed In His Own Word
summary: William Branham preaches on the Bible as the ultimate revelation of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that it is not a book of systems or morals but the Word of God. He warns against misinterpreting, misplacing, or dislocating Scripture, and stresses the importance of the Word as the tie post for the soul.

title: A Thinking Man's Filter
summary: William Branham uses the slogan 'A thinking man's filter, a smoking man's taste' from a cigarette pack as a metaphor for the deceptive filters of the world and denominations. He contrasts these with God's Filter, which is His Word, that separates true believers from worldly desires. The sermon emphasizes that only through the Word can one be cleansed and have a holy taste.

title: Satan's Eden
summary: William Branham preaches on the deceitfulness of Satan in the last days, comparing Satan's Eden of sin and perverted religion to God's original Eden of holiness. He warns against intellectualism and man-made theology that lead people away from the pure Word of God, emphasizing that every seed brings forth after its kind and that the true church must be established on faith in God's promises.
themes: The Word of God as Seed

title: God's Power to Transform
summary: William Branham speaks at a Full Gospel Business Men's Fellowship meeting in Phoenix, Arizona, following the death of Sister Florence Shakarian. He uses Romans 12:1-2 to discuss God's transforming power versus Satan's deforming power, tracing the conflict from Eden to the present age of science and civilization.

title: Thirst
summary: William Branham preaches on the natural and spiritual thirst for God, using Psalm 42 as a text. He contrasts the God-given thirst for righteousness with the perversions of that thirst in a modern, hybridized age. Branham warns against satisfying spiritual thirst with worldly substitutes and emphasizes that only a living relationship with God can truly quench the soul's longing.
themes: the Holy Spirit as a guide
the need for genuine spiritual satisfaction

title: Power Of Transformation
summary: William Branham speaks on the power of transformation through renewing the mind according to God's Word. He contrasts God's original creation with Satan's deformation through civilization, urging believers to be transformed rather than conformed to the world.

title: Leadership
summary: William Branham speaks to children and adults about the importance of choosing the right leader in life, contrasting the rich young ruler who rejected Jesus with Moses who chose to follow God. He emphasizes that while education, money, and religion are good, only Jesus Christ can give eternal life.

title: What House Will You Build Me?
summary: William Branham speaks at the Tucson Tabernacle, emphasizing that God does not dwell in temples made with hands but in the body of believers. He encourages the congregation to support Brother Pearry Green's ministry and to remain faithful in the last days.

title: The Invisible Union of the Bride of Christ
summary: William Branham delivers a Thanksgiving message on the invisible union of the Bride of Christ, using Romans 7 to illustrate the Church's relationship to Christ versus the law and the world. He warns against spiritual adultery—mixing creed and denomination with the Word of God—and calls the Church to remain virgin to the Word, as a woman is to remain virtuous to her husband.

title: Works Is Faith Expressed
summary: William Branham teaches that faith is a revelation from God and must be expressed through works, using Abraham as an example. He contrasts Paul's justification by faith with James's justification by works, showing that works demonstrate the faith God has revealed. The sermon also includes testimonies of healings and prophecies, particularly about judgment on Los Angeles.

title: I Have Heard But Now I See
summary: William Branham preaches from Job 42:5, exploring how Job's faith was tested and how he moved from hearing about God to seeing Him. Branham emphasizes the importance of genuine revelation, patience in trials, and the need for right motives in prayer.

title: God's Only Provided Place of Worship
summary: William Branham preaches that God has only one place where He will meet worshippers, and that place is where He chooses to put His name. He warns against vain worship based on denominational creeds and emphasizes the need to follow God's Word exactly, using examples from Cain and Abel, Balaam and Moses, and Martha and Mary.
themes: God's only provided place of worship

title: On The Wings Of A Snow-White Dove
summary: William Branham preaches on the symbolism of the dove in Scripture, drawing parallels between the dove's nature and the Christian life. He discusses the dove's cleanliness, lack of gall, and its role in sacrifice and as a sign of peace, culminating in the Holy Spirit descending as a dove at Jesus' baptism.
themes: Dove as symbol of the Holy Spirit
Cleanliness and purity of the Christian

title: The Rapture
summary: William Branham speaks on the Rapture of the Church, emphasizing that it is a revelation for the Bride of Christ. He discusses the scoffers of the last days, the vindication of God's Word, and the predestination of believers. He urges the audience to recognize the signs of the times and prepare for Christ's coming.

title: Modern Events Are Made Clear By Prophecy
summary: William Branham preaches on how modern events are clarified by biblical prophecy, emphasizing the need for the church to return to the pure Word of God and warning against denominationalism and worldliness. He discusses the progression of church ages and the coming of the Bride age, calling believers to be separated and ready for Christ's return.

title: Communion
summary: William Branham speaks on the sacredness of Communion, emphasizing that it must be taken with sincerity and understanding, not as a mere tradition. He explains that Communion, along with water baptism and feet-washing, are the three physical ordinances left to the Church, and that they symbolize the believer's identification with Christ's death and resurrection.
